newsitem.title: FINLAND: Amer CFO departure may help-analysts.
newsitem.headline: Amer CFO departure may help-analysts.

text.p: The resignation of Kari Miettinen, executive vice president and CFO of Finnish sporting goods group Amer-yhtyma Oy, should help restructuring at the loss-making company, analysts said on Tuesday.
"It will give Amer CEO Roger Talermo room to work," said Martti Larjo of Merita Bank.

But they said Amer, which fell to a pre-tax loss of 206 million markka in January-August and has said its full-year 1996 result will clearly be in the red, would need to do more than switch its CFO -- as the company announced on Tuesday -- to restore confidence.
"We'll have to see clear signs of a turnaround in performance," said Terho Mussalo of FSB Securities. "There are no tricks to restoring confidence."

"Results are what is needed," Larjo said, adding that he would be watching next year for the outcome of the restructuring of the Wilson golf and tennis equipment unit, and to the impact of new products on its Atomic ski and skate unit.
In November, Amer said it would target a break-even result in 1997.

Amer announced the sale its MacGregor golf unit in October and of its Finland-based car dealerships in November, but it has said the rebuild of its Wilson unit, accounting for 60 percent of January-October group net sales, will take time.
"(The resignation) may help clarify the situation there," said Ritva Ojala at Aktia Bank, adding she believed Amer's break-even forecast was "in the right direction."
But Merita's Larjo said: "It will be a tough job to get back into positive ground next year."
